dossier.purpose: Prometheus (CNCF project, v3.15.0, Apache-2.0) is a single-binary Go monitoring server and time-series database. It scrapes metrics from HTTP targets, stores samples in a local on-disk TSDB, evaluates PromQL recording/alerting rules, notifies Alertmanager, and serves a built-in query/graph web UI plus a stable JSON HTTP API (default 0.0.0.0:9090). Push-style ingestion is optional and off by default: a remote-write receiver and an OTLP/HTTP receiver that accepts metrics only (POST /api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics). Facts relevant to the stated needs: it is not an OpenTelemetry Collector (no receiver/processor/exporter pipeline, no redaction or filter stage, no OTLP/gRPC listener); it has no OTLP logs/events or traces ingestion and no store for them; its UI explores only its own PromQL/TSDB data (no saved-dashboard feature in the UI source); it has no trace/dataset/experiment store; and the repo contains no model-serving, LLM, MCP, Claude Code or Codex code (searched). All findings come from reading source and docs at the pinned commit; nothing was built or run.

claims.claim: Prometheus, a CNCF project, is a systems and service monitoring system. It collects metrics from configured targets at given intervals, evaluates rule expressions, displays the results, and can trigger alerts when specified conditions are observed.
Distinguishing features: a multi-dimensional data model (time series defined by metric name and key/value dimensions) and PromQL, a powerful and flexible query language.
No dependency on distributed storage; single server nodes are autonomous.
An HTTP pull model for time series collection; pushing time series is supported via an intermediary gateway for batch jobs.
Multiple modes of graphing and dashboarding support.
Support for hierarchical and horizontal federation.
Precompiled binaries for released versions are on prometheus.io/download; using the latest production release binary is the recommended way to install Prometheus.
Docker images are on Quay.io and Docker Hub; 'docker run --name prometheus -d -p 127.0.0.1:9090:9090 prom/prometheus' makes Prometheus reachable at http://localhost:9090/.
Building from source needs Go (version in go.mod or greater), NodeJS (version in web/ui/.nvmrc or greater) and npm 10+; 'make build' compiles the web assets in so Prometheus can run from anywhere.
With plain 'go install', Prometheus reads web assets from web/ui/static and must be run from the repo root; the React UI is not included unless built with make assets or make build.
Service discovery plugins can be excluded at build time with the tag remove_all_sd and re-enabled individually with enable_<name>_sd; file_sd, static_sd and http_sd are always kept.
prometheus/prometheus builds a stand-alone program and is not designed for use as a library; no care has been taken to make it work well as one.
The Remote Write protobuf is published independently at buf.build (experimental); Go module tags v0.3y.z mirror v3.y.z releases.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No phone-home, analytics or update-check code found: grep of *.go/*.md/*.yml for telemetry, phone-home, analytics and update-check hits only OpenTelemetry library imports and doc text; the README says nothing about telemetry or OTLP. 'Telemetry' in flag help means Prometheus's own /metrics endpoint (docs/command-line/prometheus.md:17; web/web.go:502). Web UI sources load no remote scripts, fonts or analytics (web/ui/mantine-ui/index.html:20-36; grep of web/ui found none). Inbound: one HTTP listener, default 0.0.0.0:9090, serving UI, API, /metrics, /federate and consoles (cmd/prometheus/main.go:432-433; web/web.go:501-508, 744-783); no authentication or TLS unless --web.config.file is given and that feature is marked EXPERIMENTAL (main.go:444-447; docs/configuration/https.md:6-7); CORS origin default is '.*' (main.go:497-498); lifecycle API, admin API, remote-write receiver and OTLP receiver are all off by default (main.go:470-486). The OTLP receiver is HTTP-only on that same port; there is no 4317/4318 listener or gRPC server code (ports 4317/4318 appear only as tracing-exporter test endpoints: config/config_test.go:1839, tracing/tracing_test.go:124). Outbound connections occur only for configured features: scrape targets, service-discovery providers (cloud/API credentials when configured), Alertmanager, remote_write/remote_read, and an OTLP trace exporter for Prometheus's own spans only if tracing.endpoint is set (sampling_fraction defaults to 0, insecure defaults to false) (tracing/tracing.go:86-93; docs/configuration/configuration.md:4254-4287). The default config scrapes only localhost:9090 and lists no Alertmanager (documentation/examples/prometheus.yml:7-33). No account or hosted service is required to run it. Build/CI network use: Go modules and pnpm packages (Makefile:62-68) and, for non-GO_ONLY make test, scripts/check-go-mod-version.sh queries go.dev (scripts/check-go-mod-version.sh:9-13).

code.architecture: Single Go process. cmd/prometheus/main.go parses flags and wires components in an oklog run.Group (:1269-1658): scrape and notify discovery managers (discovery/*, providers registered through plugins/*.go) feed the scrape manager (scrape/); samples go through ready/fanout storage (storage/) into the local TSDB (tsdb/: head, WAL, blocks, compaction, out-of-order window; opened at main.go:1497-1545) or, with --agent, a WAL-only agent store (tsdb/agent; main.go:1555-1613) plus optional remote write/read clients (storage/remote/). The rule manager (rules/) evaluates PromQL (promql/, grammar promql/parser/generated_parser.y) and the notifier (notifier/) sends alerts to Alertmanager. Config is YAML in config/ (reload via SIGHUP or /-/reload); data model in model/; protobuf in prompb/. Web layer: web/web.go (router, UI assets, federation, consoles, single http.Server via exporter-toolkit) and web/api/v1/api.go (JSON API). UI: web/ui/mantine-ui (default) and web/ui/react-app (old UI via --enable-feature=old-ui) with web/ui/module/{codemirror-promql,lezer-promql}. OTLP receiver path: web/api/v1/api.go:381-388,490 -> storage/remote/write_otlp_handler.go (optional OTel Collector deltatocumulative processor, :86-109) -> storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite (derived from opentelemetry-collector-contrib, metrics_to_prw.go:13-15) -> AppenderV2 into the TSDB; self-metrics prometheus_api_otlp_* at write_otlp_handler.go:76-81, 249-259. Also: compliance/ (remote-write compliance tests), documentation/ (examples, Grafana-dashboard mixin for monitoring Prometheus itself), internal/tools (tool dependencies).

benchmarks.what: Average on-disk TSDB storage per ingested sample (no workload or hardware stated)
TSDB chunk population per-sample overhead reduction (release 3.13.0)
Case-insensitive prefix matching for long case-insensitive regexes (release 3.13.0)
V2 histogram WAL decoder allocation reduction for native histograms with created-timestamp storage (release 3.13.0)
benchmarks.value: up to 50% fewer allocations, up to 10% less memory

risks: Scope gap on OTLP signals: the only OTLP ingestion route is POST /api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics (web/api/v1/api.go:490) and the docs call it the OTLP Metrics receiver (docs/querying/api.md:1880-1891). No OTLP logs/events or traces handler, no OTLP/gRPC server and no logs or traces store exist in the code (grep for plog, ptrace, plogotlp, ptraceotlp, /v1/logs, /v1/traces, grpc.NewServer found none); the only OTLP traces code exports Prometheus's own spans (tracing/tracing.go:131-175). The repo also has no dataset/experiment store, model server, GPU code, MCP server or Claude Code/Codex integration.

No privacy filter or redaction stage on the OTLP path: every datapoint attribute becomes a label and only __name__ is skipped (storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite/helper.go:65-70, 95-100; number_data_points.go:42-50); all non-identifying resource attributes are written to target_info (helper.go:533-579) and DisableTargetInfo is never set outside tests (metrics_to_prw_test.go:79). The otlp: settings only choose which resource attributes are additionally promoted to labels and how names are translated (config/config.go:1770-1816); relabeling is not applied to OTLP ingestion (no relabel code in write_otlp_handler.go; metric_relabel_configs is a scrape setting, docs/configuration/configuration.md:3681-3685). Attribute values therefore land as labels in the TSDB and WAL on local disk.

Delta-temporality metrics are rejected by default: the converter errors with 'invalid temporality and type combination' (metrics_to_prw.go:288-297) and, from reading the handler, any converter error rolls back the whole request and returns HTTP 500 (write_otlp_handler.go:147-155, 203-206; not executed), so a mixed payload fails entirely. Delta support is optional and experimental: otlp-deltatocumulative keeps in-memory state that is lost on restart (counter reset) and is mutex-guarded; otlp-native-delta-ingestion ignores StartTimeUnixNano and stores deltas with unknown type (docs/feature_flags.md:204-223); the two flags are mutually exclusive (cmd/prometheus/main.go:361-363).

The OTLP receiver is documented as low-volume and is strict about ordering: 'not considered an efficient way of ingesting samples... specific low-volume use cases' (docs/querying/api.md:1882-1885); out-of-order, duplicate-timestamp and too-old samples are rejected with HTTP 400 (write_otlp_handler.go:199-202) and the out-of-order window defaults to 0s (docs/configuration/configuration.md:4176; the upstream OTLP example sets 30m, documentation/examples/prometheus-otlp.yml:28-31); attribute churn can cause high memory use (docs/configuration/configuration.md:246); metadata of OTLP metrics is not served by /api/v1/metadata or the UI metrics explorer (docs/querying/api.md:1187; web/api/v1/api.go:1602-1606). No published OTLP ingest throughput or latency figures were found.

Network exposure and auth defaults: listens on 0.0.0.0:9090 (cmd/prometheus/main.go:432-433); no authentication or TLS unless an EXPERIMENTAL web config file is supplied (main.go:444-447; docs/configuration/https.md:6-7; docs/stability.md:29); CORS origin defaults to '.*' (main.go:497-498); the OTLP receiver shares this listener (web/web.go:744-783). The README Docker example binds to 127.0.0.1 (README.md:60) but the Dockerfile only declares EXPOSE 9090 (Dockerfile:27).

Platform and storage constraints: the TSDB needs a local POSIX filesystem and NFS (including EFS) is unsupported (docs/storage.md:129-133; warning at cmd/prometheus/main.go:1516-1518); default retention is 15d so older data is deleted unless configured (docs/storage.md:94-96); single node with no replication (docs/storage.md:59-63); Agent mode disables local queries and storage (docs/prometheus_agent.md:16, 28). WSL2 is neither documented nor tested upstream, GPU is not applicable, and CI test jobs run only on Linux and Windows (ci.yml:15, 181).

Maintenance and build drift: minor releases roughly every 6 weeks (RELEASE.md:7; 3.15.0 dated 2026-09-24 at CHANGELOG.md:5) with older minor branches maintained best-effort (RELEASE.md:59); the 3.14.0 changelog lists several TSDB data-loss and crash fixes (CHANGELOG.md:121-127). README build prerequisites are stale: UI builds use pnpm not npm (Makefile:62-68), go.mod says Go 1.26.0 while release builds use 1.27 (go.mod:3; .promu.yml:4), NOTICE references a react-app/package-lock.json that no longer exists (NOTICE:111), and documentation/internal_architecture.md code links are for v2.3.1 (:11). Source builds need Go plus a Node/pnpm toolchain because the UI is built from source (Makefile:112-118).

Supply-chain and release verification: no checksum, signature, attestation or SBOM step is visible in this repo's workflows or Makefiles; artifact publishing is delegated to an external pinned action (prometheus/promci/publish_release, ci.yml:425) that was not inspected; RELEASE.md only says GPG-signing the git tag is appreciated (RELEASE.md:161). CodeQL analyzes JavaScript only (codeql-analysis.yml:22); SECURITY-INSIGHTS.yml expired 2025-07-30 (:3); Dependabot config is scripts/dependabot.yml with no .github/dependabot.yml in the tree and minor/patch Dependabot PRs get auto-merge enabled (automerge-dependabot.yml:26-27); Docker base images use a floating tag (Dockerfile:3 uses :latest; Dockerfile.distroless:4 is tag-pinned only). Dependency footprint: 109 direct and 140 indirect Go modules including many cloud SDKs (go.mod:5-264). Licensing: project is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE); transitive dependency licenses were not audited.
